clue.text: Defiant Iran tests resolution

indicators.note: a resolution breaks something down into its parts, so these letters are separated and reassembled

explanation.surface: A rebellious Iran pushes ahead with weapons tests despite a UN resolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like a UN motion, but it signals the letters of IRAN TESTS being resolved into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resisting authority is openly defiant, standing firm against pressure.

clue.text: Serving up beer and gin cocktail

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for beer is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mix, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: A barman is serving drinks: beer and a gin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to entertain them lavishly with food and drink, i.e. to serve them.

clue.text: Boil on range, say, in this?

definitions.text: Boil on range, say, in this?

parts.words: Boil on range, say, in this?
parts.note: boiling something on a kitchen range calls for a cooking pot with a handle; boil and range also suggest a skin spot and mountains

explanation.surface: A question about where to boil something on the kitchen range.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan with a long handle is the usual vessel for boiling on a cooker hob.

clue.text: Wind tears up almost everything

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for tears is read upwards

parts.note: tears (rips) means rips

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word for everything

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A gale tears up nearly everything in its path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' is not weeping but rips; turned up it gives SPIR, then AL is ALL without its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to coil or curl round, the verb sense of a corkscrew shape.

clue.text: A fellow before robbery's nervous

parts.note: a raid is a robbery; the 's stands for is, joining to the definition

explanation.surface: A man waiting outside before a robbery is jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scared of what might happen leaves a person nervous.

clue.text: Strategic diplomacy by first Islamic state

parts.note: tact is diplomacy in handling people

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Islamic

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for the US state of California

explanation.surface: A strategy of diplomacy towards the first Islamic state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactical and strategic are close synonyms describing planned manoeuvres.

clue.text: Outburst delivered in a nasal voice

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words a nasal voice

explanation.surface: An outburst delivered in a whiny, nasal voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' is padding for the surface; 'in' alone points to the letters inside A NASAL VOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of gunfire, figuratively a sudden volley of words.

clue.text: Pathetic one attached to sound punishment is!

definitions.text: Pathetic one attached to sound punishment is!

parts.note: pathetic means sad
one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: sound tells us to write a word that is pronounced like the word for punishment

parts.note: stick is informal for punishment or harsh criticism

explanation.surface: A remark that anyone fond of administering beatings is a sorry creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning thorough, but it signals a homophone: STIC is said like STICK. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitiable person devoted to inflicting pain is the very picture of cruelty for pleasure.

clue.text: Left with single pound to spend

parts.note: single gives I, the Roman numeral one
quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone is left with just one pound in their pocket to spend.
explanation.walkthrough: QUID is British slang for one pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid assets are cash readily available for spending.

clue.text: Originally Blair's old right, all right?

parts.note: well can mean in good health, all right

explanation.surface: A question about whether Blair's old right-wing politics were acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair looks like Tony Blair, but the writer George Orwell was born Eric Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist of 1984 used a pen name; his birth surname was Blair.

clue.text: Flasher German car's inside

indicators.note: inside places the car make within the abbreviation for German

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker

explanation.surface: A man flashes from inside a German car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flasher' suggests an exhibitionist, but it means more flashy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudier means more showy, i.e. flashier.

clue.text: Credit note

definitions.meaning: to credit a work to someone is to ascribe it to them
a note can be a quality or feature, as in a note of sadness

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means credit or ascribe; as a noun it means a characteristic or distinctive note.

clue.text: Stuck by motorway returning on dim day

indicators.note: returning means the motorway abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI
pale means dim or faint

explanation.surface: A driver stuck on the motorway, heading back on a gloomy day.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaled means pierced and stuck on a point.

clue.text: Keep funny dialect

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of dialect are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keep up that amusing regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun: a castle's stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the central tower of a castle, a fortress or stronghold.

clue.text: Opportunity to put a cross into the box?

definitions.text: Opportunity to put a cross into the box?

parts.words: Opportunity to put a cross into the box?
parts.note: sounds like a football cross into the penalty box, but really means marking an X in a box on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A winger sees a chance to send a cross into the penalty area.
explanation.definitionFit: At a national vote, electors mark a cross beside a candidate on a ballot.

clue.text: The right response

definitions.meaning: the conservative wing in politics, opposed to progress
a reply or answer to something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a political backlash towards conservatism and any reply to a stimulus.

clue.text: Cut cost — on a shoestring

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means one piece sits above the other, so cost follows shoestring

parts.note: a lace is a shoestring
a rate is a cost or charge

explanation.surface: Costs are cut because the business runs on a shoestring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a shoestring' looks like a phrase for frugal, but the shoestring is LACE, with RATE placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to cut or tear the flesh.

clue.text: Cheeky monkey's on fire, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the letters are what certain words sound like when spoken

parts.note: a mischievous child is a monkey or imp; on fire is alight; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A cheeky monkey has set himself alight, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: IMP ALIGHT, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky behaviour is rude or discourteous.

clue.text: Most crackers or bananas?

parts.note: crackers and bananas both mean mad, but suggest snacks; the most crazy also hints at the food that is fullest of kernels

explanation.surface: A question about which snack is best: crackers or bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is slang for crazy, so the superlative means the most mad.

clue.text: Obsolete mysterious agency's back

parts.note: arch means knowing or sly, with a secretive air

indicators.note: back means the letters of the agency are written in reverse

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: An outdated, secretive intelligence agency returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to an earlier time, out of date.

clue.text: Pitfall of America's end of term president

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for America

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of term

parts.note: Bush was the name of two US presidents

explanation.surface: A trap waiting for an American president at the end of his term.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack, a trap or pitfall laid for the unwary.

clue.text: Conservative's more worn out — more distant

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
older means more aged and worn

explanation.surface: An aging Tory grows more aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooler manner is less friendly, more aloof and distant.

clue.text: Stickler for force on American position

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
a spot is a position or place

explanation.surface: A pedant insists on forcing an American position.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is someone overly particular about details, a stickler.

clue.text: He's a lumberjack…

parts.note: a lumberjack cuts down trees, and the word for such a person is also slang for a chap

explanation.surface: Quoting the opening of a comic song about a lumberjack.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fells trees is also, in colloquial speech, a fellow or chap.

clue.text: Put an end to drink

definitions.meaning: to stop or quash a rumour

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to quash a rumour; the noun is whisky distilled north of the border.

clue.text: Liberal at variance between two parties

indicators.note: at variance means in disagreement, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A Liberal at odds in a two-party arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' does two things in the surface but here is part of the fodder, with 'at variance' the indicator only by its second word... the whole of LIBERAL AT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral describes an agreement involving two sides.

clue.text: One's trapped in broken cattle grid

indicators.note: trapped in means one piece sits inside the other
broken means the letters of cattle are rearranged

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An animal is caught in a broken cattle grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns CATTLE into LATTCE, and 'trapped in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a framework of crossing strips, a grid.

clue.text: The woman's no flipping bird!

parts.note: her means belonging to the woman

indicators.note: flipping means the word no is turned around

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that the woman is certainly no bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild curse but reverses NO into ON; 'bird' also teases British slang for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Operating theatre is most dirty

indicators.note: operating means working on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The operating theatre is the dirtiest place in the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating theatre' reads as a hospital room, but 'Operating' is the anagram signal working on THEATRE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthiest means most soiled with earth, i.e. grubbiest.
